column4: Visit note | 2025-08-16 10:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Taslima Sarkar, 26, female. Mrs. Sarkar returns for a review of her skin, mentioning she still has spots on her back, marks left after pimples, and pimples and blackheads on her face. Her condition has been worse since working in a hot kitchen in Farmgate. She works as a delivery rider. She reports no fever and no other systemic complaints. On examination: about 19 inflamed spots on the face, BP 114/74 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 70 kg. Her skin shows persistent inflammatory papules and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and do not squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-08-17 04:30 PM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Shyamal Bose, 49, male. Mr. Bose presents for his first visit complaining of a ring-shaped itchy red rash, a rash with spreading edges, and itch worse in humid weather. He states that the trouble started after playing football on wet fields in Cox's Bazar. He works as a textile engineer and mentions spending long hours outdoors in damp clothing. He has no known chronic illnesses such as diabetes. He denies any recent travel abroad, joint pains, or other skin eruptions. On examination: affected area about 7 cm across, BP 128/81 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 57 kg. The lesion on his upper trunk shows an active, raised, erythematous, scaly border with central clearing. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued today to treat the fungal infection effectively. He was strongly advised to keep the skin dry, avoid sharing towels with family members, and wash all his clothes in hot water to prevent reinfection. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
